name: Solage, Auberge Collection
positioning: Cottage-style Auberge Collection resort with a geothermal spa, in Calistoga at the quieter end of Napa Valley
best_for: Travelers who want private cottage-style rooms with their own outdoor space
Guests planning a spa and wine-country stay in quiet Calistoga

facts.text: Solage is in Calistoga, at the quieter end of Napa Valley.
The property is laid out like a series of modern farmhouse neighborhoods with low whitewashed buildings and gravel paths.
Even the entry-level studios have their own patio.
Spa Solage's Bathhouse is fed by Calistoga's geothermal springs and has hydrotherapy pools, a steam room, a sauna and a cold plunge.
Solbar is the main restaurant, with a seasonal, locally driven menu.
The resort announced a resort-wide redesign in May 2021.
Solage received the Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star Award in February 2020.
The mostly single-story, spread-out design makes navigation relatively straightforward, and accessible accommodations are available upon request.

highlights.text: Accommodation is built around standalone cottages.
The Bathhouse at Spa Solage is fed by Calistoga's geothermal springs and has hydrotherapy pools, a steam room, a sauna and a cold plunge.
Many rooms include outdoor showers, fire pits and garden space.
Picobar is a poolside restaurant serving modern Mexican food with tostadas, tacos and mezcal cocktails.

considerations.text: The pool is lively and not particularly quiet.
Minibars are fully stocked but all items are chargeable.
Check-in delays have been known to happen at arrival.
